title: Submodular Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Effective Online Distributed Task Allocation
claim: Real-world distributed allocation is an open system where agents and tasks arrive and depart under limited communication and sensing.
layout: single panel scene with legend on right; dashed circles, red event labels
description: A single schematic scene of mobile sensors (black drones) that track moving targets (orange drones). Each sensor has a light-blue shaded sensing zone with a gray cone pointing toward a target. A dashed blue circle around each sensor marks its communication range. Teal double-headed arrows join sensors whose ranges overlap. Dashed black arrows show target trajectories. Red bold labels mark dynamic events: 'Agent departure/broken' (a drone with a red X), 'Agent arrival' (a sensor with a starburst), and 'Task arrival' (a new target with a starburst). A gray legend box on the right explains Moving Target, Mobile Sensor, Communication Range and Sensing Zone. The eye goes first to the overlapping circles and the red event labels.
caption: An open multi-agent system for task allocation. Mobile sensors collaboratively track mobile targets under time-varying agent populations, dynamic tasks, limited communication, and bounded sensing.
abstract: This paper studies online distributed multi-agent task allocation with submodular team utilities. Since each agent selects one action from a local categorical distribution, feasible joint actions form a partition matroid over agent-action pairs. The classical Multilinear Extension relaxation, based on independent Bernoulli sampling, does not align with categorical execution under partition-matroid constraints. To remedy this, we propose the Partition Multilinear Extension (PME), which equals the expected stage utility under factorized categorical policies. We prove that submodular difference rewards provide unbiased PME marginal-gradient information and a stagewise policy-gradient estimator. Building on this connection, we propose SubMAPG, a centralized-training, decentralized-execution framework using masked categorical policies and difference-reward signals. For projected stochastic-gradient ascent in the PME marginal space, we establish a stagewise 1/2-approximation guarantee and sublinear dynamic regret under slowly varying environments. We instantiate SubMAPG on graph neural network policy models that effectively handle open systems with time-varying agents and tasks. Experiments on cooperative coverage and multi-target tracking showcase superior performance compared with standard MARL that does not leverage submodular rewards, online submodular optimization, and greedy baselines.
